chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"When the redness disappears from this side, meaning from the direction of the East, the sun has set from the East of the Earth and from its West."

key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: The redness in the sky after sunset, a key indicator for prayer times.
key_terms.الْمَشْرِق: The East, the direction from which the sun rises.

ai.seo_question: How is the exact time for Maghrib prayer determined according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the specific boundary for Maghrib prayer, distinguishing it from the general sunset. The Imam emphasizes the simultaneity of the sun's setting across the globe by noting that the disappearance of the eastern redness (al-humrah) signifies the sun has set in both the East and West, providing a practical astronomical marker for worshippers. This definition is crucial in Shia fiqh for determining the exact onset of the Maghrib time window.
